title: Come to the Waters
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Why spend yourself on what doesn't satisfy? God doesn't just say stop. He offers a far better feast: Jesus, our greatest delight.
exhortation: Jesus, open our eyes to the poison we're drinking without even realizing it's poison. Isn't it true that we all drift toward foolish habits that satisfy for about a microsecond?

This morning, ask yourself: what am I spending my life on that returns no real, lasting reward? It could be as simple as food, numbing pain, or what we all seem prone to these days, the endless scroll. Habits born of plain boredom. Paul asks in Romans 6:21, "What fruit were you getting at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death."
Christian, shed the sins of your past. In Christ you are a new creation. You are not enslaved to your sins anymore. Don't go back to them. Instead, put your faith fully in Jesus.

Notice the instruction here. God doesn't tell us to starve ourselves. It isn't just "stop doing those things." Just like the exhortation Jonathan gave yesterday, there is a put-off, but there is a much better put-on: "Eat what is good, and delight yourselves in rich food." The promise in Christ is not a lesser joy but a greater one. Jesus came to free you from slavery to sin, from the empty bread we're so tempted to go back to that consumes our strength but never satisfies. In Jesus is our greatest delight. So today, Lord, help us fix our eyes on you, our greatest joy.
prayer: Lord, this is our hope and our longing: to see you face to face and hear you say, "Well done, good and faithful servant." And yet we recognize that we are weak and needy, so we cry out for help and for grace. We cry out for the power of your Holy Spirit to fill us, guide our steps, keep us on the path and bring us home to glory.
We say this in faith, because you promised to be with us and bring us home. So we say it with joy, faith and hope in our hearts. In your precious name, amen.
